ig_carousel_topic.topic: Player props vs. game lines: different math, different edges
ig_carousel_topic.slide1_text:
Props vs. Game Lines
Same sport. Different math.
Most bettors treat them the same. That's the mistake.
ig_carousel_topic.slide2_text:
The common assumption:
'A good team bet means their props are good too.'
Not how it works. Props and game lines price two completely different things.
ig_carousel_topic.slide3_text:
Game lines price the outcome of 9 innings or 48 minutes. Props price one player's stat in one slice of that game.
Different sample. Different variance. Different edge sources.
ig_carousel_topic.slide4_text:
Real example: a pitcher's strikeout prop might be set at 6.5. The book prices it off recent K-rate and opponent strikeout percentage. The game line on the same team could be -180. Those two numbers have almost no relationship to each other.
You can bet the under on that prop and the team ML. Both can win. Both can lose. Independently.
ig_carousel_topic.slide5_text:
The edge in props comes from stat-model mismatches, not from picking winners. The edge in game lines comes from pricing inefficiencies across books.
Learn which game you're playing before you place the bet.
ig_carousel_topic.caption: Props and game lines are priced on different inputs. Knowing which edge applies where is what separates sharp bettors from guessers.
